channel.title: Diya Subedi — Poems
channel.description: Nepali poems in English and Nepali, written and narrated by Diya Subedi.

item.title: Kayeu Chan Timro Lagi Pani
item.description: A Nepali spoken-word poem about heartbreak, and all the people who still hold you without you knowing it.

item.title: Bilauney Chan Yi Yaad Haru
item.description: A Nepali poem about leaving school — the classroom, the friends, and the teacher who taught me the alphabet.

item.title: Haraeka Aasha Ani Aastha
item.description: A Nepali spoken-word poem about faith used to control people, and the families who suffer for it.

item.title: Samjhanako Sajh
item.description: A Nepali poem about dreams that didn't come true, and how an ending can still carry a new beginning.

item.title: Tuteka Tara
item.description: A Nepali spoken-word poem about memory, death, and what is left of a person when everyone who remembers them is gone.

item.title: Smritiko Jhyalale Sanchera Rakheko Hawa
item.description: A Nepali poem about the love that stays after the person leaves — memory, devotion, and what it means to still carry someone.

item.title: Swarthi Sarkar
item.description: A Nepali spoken-word poem about a government that counts votes but not bodies, and the families who are left waiting.

item.title: Chad Ki Chakku?
item.description: A Nepali poem about Dashain and the people who aren't celebrating — migrant families, fear, and what festivals forget.

item.title: I Don't Pray to God Anymore
item.description: A spoken-word poem about praying for the strength to begin again, instead of for an easier life.

item.title: The Way I Loved
item.description: A spoken-word poem about love that didn't last and changed you anyway — kindness, rain, and a candle in the wind.

item.title: Too Busy To Glow
item.description: A spoken-word poem about Tihar, marigolds, and how easy it is to rush past the light.

item.title: Ko Hau Timi?
item.description: A Nepali spoken-word poem about identity — the rivers, the rain, and the question of what you are remembered for.

item.title: Birsine Bhayen
item.description: A Nepali poem about an unfinished goodbye, and the love that becomes memory instead of disappearing.

item.title: I Love Love
item.description: A spoken-word poem about the small, unromantic ways people love each other — a meme, a seat, a favorite color remembered.

item.title: Antim Saajh
item.description: A Nepali poem about borrowed homes and borrowed skies — evening, rivers, and the things that were never ours to keep.

item.title: An Ordinary Dayy
item.description: A spoken-word poem about perspective — someone's worst day is someone else's best, and every street holds a story.

item.title: Kaha Chha Ra Khusi?
item.description: A Nepali spoken-word poem about searching for happiness where grief, poverty, and death live side by side.

item.title: Mero Desh, Timi Feri Uthnu Chha
item.description: A Nepali spoken-word poem about sacrifice and hope — a country that has waited, and the belief that it will rise again.

item.title: It Never Did
item.description: A spoken-word poem about death, being forgotten, and the realization that the moments still matter even when the name doesn't.
